# Machine learning with JAX: functional patterns, JIT, and core practices

Curated by Skill Harbor — @mindrally's machine-learning skill: a lightweight JAX reference for agents writing ML code in a functional style. Covers JAX fundamentals — jax.numpy for NumPy-compatible ops, automatic differentiation with jax.grad, JIT compilation with jax.jit, vectorization with jax.vmap — plus JAX-native control flow (jax.lax.scan, cond, fori_loop; no Python control flow inside jitted functions), functional random numbers (proper key splitting, never reuse keys), pytrees for nested structures, custom vjp/jvp, sharding for multi-device training, checkpointing, and model-development pointers (pure functions, Flax or Haiku layers, proper initialization, functional training loops). Honest caveats: a lightweight reference, not a tutorial — no worked examples, no helper scripts, thin on guidance for when things go wrong; strictly JAX-focused (not a general ML methodology). Apache-2.0 licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
